belief: If I'm not healed, I must not be right with God.
origins: Some equate health with God’s favor and illness with distance from Him. Without healing, we may scour our lives for hidden sin or doubt our salvation.
teaches: “Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus” (Romans 8:1). Right standing with God comes by grace through faith in Christ, not by health. Paul, Timothy, Epaphroditus, and Trophimus were all faithful and all sick at times. “Neither this man nor his parents sinned,” said Jesus of the blind man. Paul’s promise that nothing “will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord” includes illness. Health is a blessing, but it is not the proof of God’s favor.
self_statements: Healthy people are in good standing with God.
I should be healed if I were right.
errors: Believing health shows favor and illness shows disfavor.
Feeling sick and concluding that I am not right with God.
questions: What do I think healing would prove about me?

truth: My standing with God is secured by Christ, not by my health. Illness does not mean God is displeased. Nothing can separate me from His love.
hw_truths: There is no condemnation in Christ.
Nothing separates me from His love.
